findings.summary: A newly created scratch directory is not fsynced through its data-root parent, so the synced record can be unreachable after a crash.
Scratch creation uses default permissions rather than the data root mode, and the test does not exercise a differing data-root mode.
The synced writer truncates an occupied fixed redo-record path, allowing a leftover record to be overwritten instead of recovered.
The redo-record writer does not durably publish a newly created scratch directory, does not preserve data-root permissions, and can overwrite an existing redo record.

1. **[blocking][issue-impact][high]** `RedoRecord::commit` creates `tmp/` but fsyncs only `tmp/`, never its parent data root. When `tmp/` is absent, a crash after return can lose the parent’s directory entry and make the otherwise-synced redo record unreachable. This fails REQ-01’s durable commit point. [`crates/jit/src/storage/redo_record.rs:128`] References: `@/charter/D-17`.

2. **[blocking][issue-impact][high]** `create_dir_all` applies the process’s default creation mode filtered by umask; it does not copy the data root’s mode. A `0700` data root can therefore get a `0755` scratch directory. The added test only compares two directories created with the same default mode, so it cannot detect this REQ-03 failure. [`crates/jit/src/storage/redo_record.rs:128`] References: none.

3. **[blocking][issue-impact][high]** The new synced-write helper uses `File::create`, which truncates an occupied fixed `tmp/redo.record` path. Consequently `RedoRecord::commit` can overwrite a leftover complete record instead of preserving it for session replay, contradicting both the claimed atomic-write enforcement and D-17’s leftover-record recovery. [`crates/jit/src/storage/atomic_write.rs:59`] References: `@/invariant/atomic-writes`, `@/charter/D-17`.
